label: Wiring dilation
title: Rewiring the ring by dilation is a relabeling when the factor is coprime, a change when the observation stays put, and a split when it divides
kind: Exact audit of the program's first change of interaction graph, with theorem controls
summary: Reading the same rule table at offsets ±d instead of ±1: when d is coprime to the ring and the observation is dilated too, every census and the commutator classification are exactly preserved, because the rewiring is a site permutation. When the observation stays standard, the closed set shrinks and the observation rule leaves the commuter set, and the change equals observing the standard automaton through an inverse-offset observation. When d divides the ring, the system splits into d interleaved rings and the census, depth included, equals the small-ring census.
takeaway: A change of wiring is a coordinate change only when the whole contract travels with it; otherwise it is a real change, and the program's three verdicts sort it exactly.
